title: Application for Federal Domestic Assistance - Individual
description: Collects applicant, citizenship, project and certification information for an individual seeking federal assistance. The applicant is the individual; this edition has no organization, UEI, EIN or estimated-funding section.
notes: The applicant is the individual. Reuse the existing name, address and contact questions without adding organization, EIN, UEI or an unrequested person title. Citizenship and congressional district belong under applicant.

Five opportunity/competition fields are read-only and pre-populated by existing SGG API providers. Received date, signature and date signed are optional in draft answers and required in final submission XML; they are post-populated by the API.

Citizenship candidate follows explicit DAT5c-6/7/8 business rules: for No, alien number is optional and country/residency date are required; dependent controls are inactive for Yes. Applicant wording separately refers to permanent residents and foreign nationals. That inconsistency is recorded for review; no new three-state status is invented.

Shared Address retains the existing SGG five-digit US ZIP behavior. DAT5b-9 asks for at least nine characters; this is the existing named ZIP+4 gap, not a claim of source parity or an implicit global bank change. Foreign province/postal code remain optional; State and postal code are required for USA.

DAT6c-2/3 validation messages require end date not earlier than start date. The definition declares notBefore; the SGG emitter and API rule validator enforce it through the existing rule-processing boundary.
Certification requires an affirmative checked answer. The Yes/No XML value is derived from that Boolean; legal text and the source assurance note remain visible.
XML follows the official sequence, including applicant fax/email/phone ahead of address. Layout order is independent of answer nesting and XML order.
Samples use synthetic opportunity context and signing values so JSON/XML are inspectable before API installation. Samples do not implement population or signing.

The current SGG renderer hard-codes section heading levels. Applicant fields therefore share one visible Applicant Information section, using existing UI.flatten for name/address/citizenship and inline contact fields. JSON retains those concept groups; nested visual headings can return when the shared renderer supports them.

Opportunity owns agency, assistance listing and funding opportunity values. Date Received belongs to the application and appears in a separate Application Information section. This moves it after the opportunity fields on screen; XML retains its official sequence.

Opportunity nesting uses the existing XML-shaped mapping. The older answer-shaped XML transform cannot interleave Date Received between opportunity-owned values. When API sync is enabled, select xml: mapping; no mapper implementation change is included.
risks: Citizenship labels and DAT conditional rules disagree; the explicit-DAT candidate and rationale require source-owner review.
US postal validation accepts five digits, but the DAT requires nine. The shared Address question needs a reviewed ZIP+4 rule; this form does not introduce a private Address or change the shared rule.
The library declares the start/end date relation. The API also needs date_not_before rule support from the separate shared-support PR before this rule works in SGG.
Grantor1/training submissions, completed external PDFs and production acceptance are separate evidence gates; local checks do not satisfy them.

Changing Country can leave both State and Province in an answer. GlobalLibrary permits only one, so that answer fails XSD validation. The shared Address/retention behavior needs a reviewed fix before API submission; this form does not clear answers or change XML handling.
